page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-144-lssd is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. It features 144 virtual CPUs across 72 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The processor includes a 504 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. The system is equipped with 1116.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. Local storage consists of 24 NVMe SSDs totaling 9383 GB of capacity. No GPU resources are included.

Benchmark results place this server in the top tier for multi-core CPU and memory performance. The multi-core stress-ng CPU test scored 156,171.55, and the PassMark CPU score reached 134,938.22. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds at 11,519.35 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 205.9 GB/sec. Database operations are exceptionally strong, as demonstrated by a Redis SET performance of 219.47 million operations per second and a PassMark database operations score of 35,978.12. The server also exhibits top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing, reaching 320.19 tokens per second for a medium 7B model and 46.88 tokens per second for a large 70B model.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high resource density by combining massive memory capacity with a large local NVMe SSD storage array. This configuration reduces the need for external network-attached storage, optimizing throughput-per-resource costs for data-intensive workloads. However, a notable tradeoff is the single-core CPU performance, which falls into the average tier with a stress-ng single-core score of 2299.09, indicating that workloads relying heavily on single-threaded execution may not fully leverage the hardware's premium cost profile.

This server is designed for memory-intensive and storage-heavy enterprise workloads. It is highly suited for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and CPU-based large language model inference tasks.
